samples.question: The picture shows four solid dark patches arranged in one tight two-by-two cluster on a plain background: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right of that cluster. Each patch is a blocky shape built from small square tiles of one fixed size, and every patch is built from exactly the same number of tiles, so all four patches hold the same total dark area. A short straight coloured bar lies across each patch and cuts it into two parts, one part on each side of the bar; some bars are upright and some are flat. The dark area of a part is how much dark tile area lies on that side of the bar, which is not the same thing as how wide or how tall that side reaches. Exactly one patch is cut into two parts of equal dark area; the two equal parts of that patch have clearly different outlines, so equal area does not mean the patch looks mirrored or evenly spread about its bar. In each of the other three patches one part clearly holds more dark area than the other. The colours used, the outline shape of each patch, where the bar sits inside the patch outline, where the cluster sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which patch of the cluster is cut by its bar into two parts of equal dark area? Answer with one of: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.
